content:
tess_sales: FYI — EmpireCare dropped an RFI asking for a 4-week Dedicated POC, detailed embeddings+chat capability matrix, KMS/HSM options, SOC2/BAA proof, and an explicit overflow/fallback playbook. Attached: empire_rfi_2026.pdf. Need a draft bundle tomorrow morning.
omar_se: I can own the tech answers. Quick clarifier: do they expect streaming chat + function-calls during POC? That changes model picks and perf test shape.
nina_perf: I'll own the perf work. Please ask them for a sanitized sample (PHI redacted) or permission to run a synthetic workload that approximates their token lengths. Also need their p99 SLO target — or we can propose p99 <150ms as an anchor.
tess_sales: I'll ask for sample + SLO. Finance: can we include a provisional 4-week POC quote + conversion option to reserved capacity in the RFI?
frank_finance: Provisional pricing stub: 2x A10 baseline managed + ops support = ~$47k for 4 weeks. Include clear caveat: provisional pending final sizing/discount/legal. Mark as "provisional" in the RFI.
raj_security: Security summary for RFI: Hosted has tenant key separation and customer-provided keys in certain clouds; Private supports HSM-backed keys via partner integrations (CloudHSM, AWS Nitro HSM, YubiHSM) and requires an addendum. For PHI we need an executed BAA before ingesting PHI. I'll prepare a short KMS/HSM appendix.
legal_kim: Don't say FedRAMP authorization. Offer controls mapping and a FedRAMP-readiness plan if they ask. For SOC2, provide current Type II report for in-scope systems and a scope statement if extra systems are requested.
omar_se: Capability matrix CSV I drafted below — please review for accuracy before I paste into the RFI pack:

```
Feature,Hosted API,Dedicated Pools,Private (VPC/On-prem)
Text generation,Yes,Yes,Yes
Embeddings,Yes,Yes,Yes
Streaming chat,Limited,Yes,Yes
Private KMS,No,Yes,Yes
HSM-backed keys,No,Optional add-on,Partner integration req'd
BAA for PHI,No,Available w/ BAA,Available w/ BAA
SLA,Standard,Enhanced,Enterprise (negotiable)
Overflow/fallback,Region spill,Policy-driven failover,Policy-driven failover + notice
```

tess_sales: Nice. EmpireCare asked for a concrete fallback workflow example — can we put a 3-step example in plain language?
omar_se: Draft fallback workflow (3 steps): 1) Primary dedicated pool routes traffic; if sustained node saturation (>80% util for 90s) or queueing >5s, traffic first spills to reserved burst nodes. 2) If bursts persist, traffic fails over to a secondary dedicated pool in another region (if allowed by customer). 3) If capacity still constrained, system gracefully degrades to a smaller model variant for non-critical calls with client-visible response headers and rate-limit notifications. Admins can tune thresholds and enable automated alerts in Console.
raj_security: I'll add caveats: HSM only on Private; HSM integration timeline depends on customer environment and legal addendum. Also attach our KMS key rotation SOP and the security questionnaire link.
frank_finance: Also add billing note: POC billing can be structured as an upfront timeboxed invoice with conversion credit applied to a Reserved contract within 30 days.
legal_kim: I'll add a short paragraph on evidence we can share: current SOC2 Type II report (redacted), control mapping, and a timeline for any additional attestations. I'll also include BAA language and the need to sign before PHI transfer.
doc-bot: Uploaded: empirecare_rfi_response_draft.pdf -> https://files.redwood.internal/rfi/2955554321/empirecare_rfi_response_draft.pdf
tess_sales: Plan: I will gather the sample/SLO ask from EmpireCare, assemble the RFI pack with the capability CSV, fallback workflow, pricing stub (provisional), and attachments from @raj_security and @legal_kim. Please review here by 9am PT tomorrow. Ping me if anything blocks.
